decisions.reason: The source specifies two wings; SOL drops the quantity.
SOL keeps the sense of the sky’s emptiness in natural phrasing.
SOL keeps the contrast and overflowing image.
The em dash preserves the appositive sense.
SOL uses the established term Magic.
The source evokes a promise; SOL weakens that image to an agreement.
SOL retains the action by combining it with the following sentence.
SOL combines the staring and shouting without dropping either action.
SOL keeps the forest-in-wind image and the wave’s charge.
The source describes the killing intent as intense; SOL drops that modifier.
“Humans” keeps the contrast with the monsters.
SOL replaces the enormous scream and roar with “cheers,” changing the sound and losing its scale.
SOL preserves the notices and uses the established Fire Dragon term.
The shorter phrasing keeps the same timing.
The source says he stepped forward as if about to collapse; SOL omits that condition.
SOL naturally preserves the steam rising as he staggered onward.
SOL makes clear that the acidic substance is the blood.
“Why did you take so long?” keeps the complaint and sounds natural.
“Half melted away” preserves the extent of the damage.
SOL keeps the jewel’s location and description.
SOL keeps Morgoth’s ghastly condition despite his calm tone.
SOL keeps the denial of both lying and exaggerating.
SOL preserves the cause of the armor’s destruction and the battle’s mental toll.
“Then and there” preserves the immediacy of losing consciousness.
“Here” preserves the source’s reference to this spot.
SOL keeps the admission of good luck in a natural, spoken line.
The terse repetition keeps Morgoth’s response.
SOL keeps his quiet repetition and scrutiny of Taekyung.
SOL preserves the ragged clothes and the blood and dust covering him.
“A newborn’s” keeps the comparison while avoiding needless repetition.
The source makes the lack of healing magic a concession; SOL changes it into a separate assertion.
SOL keeps Morgoth’s doubt about luck as the explanation.
“Heaven-sent luck” keeps the claim in natural dialogue.
“Doesn’t quite sound right” keeps the sense of the expression not fitting.
BASE retains that Morgoth continued speaking as he looked toward the sunset.
SOL uses the project’s ellipsis character and preserves the beat.
SOL keeps the extraordinary healing power and the divine-favor inference.
SOL preserves God’s simultaneous closeness and distance in natural phrasing.
SOL keeps the unexpected turn and disturbance without repeating Taekyung’s name.
The source specifies that the confusion had struck for an instant; SOL drops that beat.
“Rigid” preserves Taekyung’s emotionally frozen state; “motionless” changes it to physical stillness.
“Practically” preserves the source’s sense of being almost equivalent to a divine blessing.
The fragments keep the two attributes and improve the cadence.
SOL keeps Morgoth’s exceptional standing among Dragons.
SOL reorders the sentence without changing who sought closeness to God.
SOL preserves the purpose behind both his desires and pleasures.
SOL keeps the sense of an unreserved confession.
The deleted line’s single-purpose idea is retained in the following sentence.
SOL combines the single-purpose idea with the wish to meet the creator.
SOL preserves the wasted passage of time and the everywhere-and-nowhere image.
SOL keeps Morgoth as creator, destroyer, and wanderer through the world.
“Their rules” better preserves the source’s reference to the races’ rules.
SOL preserves the forbidden realm and the pursuit of a clue without BASE’s unsupported “irredeemable.”
The source corrects “left” to “I met him”; SOL changes the subject to “we.”
The source means “If you mean him”; SOL’s “By he” is an unnatural recast.
“The earth awoke” keeps the source’s image and SOL retains Asmodeus’s title and status.
SOL preserves the silent reaction using the project’s ellipsis character.
SOL keeps the crushing helplessness and defeat in natural phrasing.
SOL preserves that Morgoth was experiencing this humiliation for the first time.
SOL keeps Morgoth’s earlier thought and the possibility he considered.
SOL preserves that Morgoth’s conjecture was wrong.
The source calls Asmodeus a powerful being; SOL’s “a power” changes the category.
“Asmodeus, of all beings” naturally preserves the source’s emphasis on serving under him.
SOL keeps the trembling eyes and Morgoth noticing them.
The source predicts that Taekyung will not understand; SOL changes the future assertion to present inability.
SOL preserves his past Dragon Lord status and his rise to second in the Demon Realm.
The source says time passed again; SOL drops the repetition.
The source says Morgoth did not find the claim funny; SOL turns his reaction into an impersonal judgment.
“It was true” preserves the confirmation.
SOL drops the source’s intensity: the Demon Realm fell into extreme chaos.
“Shaken” weakens the source’s image of everyone being thrown into turmoil.
SOL preserves the comparison between Asmodeus and every being Morgoth had encountered.
The referent is clear, and SOL preserves the news reviving interest worn down by time.
SOL keeps the Ancient Dragon’s long-awaited wish being answered today.
The source specifies both place and time: right here, today; SOL drops “today.”
“Order of things” naturally preserves the unchanging order that the being defied.
“Out of nowhere” keeps the sudden appearance, and the arms retain the landing context.
SOL preserves the contrast between Morgoth nearing death and his vivid voice and gaze.
“You who were chosen by God” works as the direct address after Morgoth’s correction.
